doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Real-life experience in jazz education
summary: Rowe values that Soskin teaches from real gig experience; Soskin says he worked hard and took advantage of opportunities.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I wonder if we’re at a point with jazz education, you know the academic level has been around long enough that sometimes we have professors who didn’t have the opportunity to actually play a lot of gigs.
And you’re bringing that as a huge part of your resume so I don’t really have a question here except to acknowledge that I think it’s really important.
That you have real-life knowledge of playing gigs and dealing with singers and everything we’ve been talking about.

Yeah dealing with the whole picture. Yeah I’ve been fortunate, I’ve been lucky enough and you know I’ve worked very hard at this. You know like well I’ve had the opportunity to play with some great people and I’ve taken advantage of it.
